The in-page browser (preview card and embedded demo) and the PDF reader are
now one shared, themeable window instead of fixed dark glass. All 23 designs
restyle it from their own visual language, and an open viewer restyles in
place when the visitor switches design.

Architecture

  status strip, plus focus trap, Esc, scroll lock and the entrance animation.
  ResumeViewer and LinkViewer keep all their behaviour and render into it.

  active and passes its font classes; each design's viewer.css is loaded with
  that design only, so a page ships its own theme, not all 23.
- The design switcher now sits above an open viewer, is part of the Tab cycle
  and Esc closes it before the viewer.

  game menu (Pixel art), a bento tray of tiles (Bento grid), a broadsheet
  masthead (Editorial), cut corners and hazard stripes (Cyberpunk), a brass
  parlour frame (Victorian), bevelled window buttons (Y2K), and so on.

Fixes found while testing
- A quick double Esc was swallowed by the viewer that was animating out.
- On short landscape phones the preview card ran off the screen; it now
  scrolls inside its window.
- Contrast fixes (status link on two themes, one chip colour).

- npm run new-design scaffolds a starter viewer.css and <ViewerTheme>.
- Unit tests require a registered theme per live design that only targets its
  own slug. e2e/viewers.spec.ts walks the card, embedded browser and PDF reader
  in every design on desktop and phone: axe, fit, tap size, focus trap,
  switching design while open, and a distinct look per design.
- README and docs/DESIGNS.md describe the system and each design's treatment.

Verified: lint, typecheck, 63 unit tests, 506 Playwright tests, a CSP run with
every viewer open in all 23 designs, and a 7-viewport audit (320px phone to
1080p, including landscape phones) of every design and viewer state.

commit.message:
feat(worker): the Cloudflare Worker and D1, phase 1 of the app plan

The shared catalog, the account layer, the IGDB proxy, the release calendar
and a ten-minute cron, on Workers Free and D1 in the EU. Deployed and seeded
with the real catalog (4,560 items) and the one user's rows. docs/worker.md is
the reference.

What runs there:
- catalog: item detail, a delta of the scoring pool, taxonomy, episodes,
  resolve-on-demand from TMDB and IGDB behind a daily fetch budget, a bulk
  lookup that never fetches, IGDB game search, one calendar month per region
- accounts: Google ID token and Trakt token sign-in, the three-outcome rule
  for an identity that already has an owner, merge with an explicit
  resolution, sessions revocable by epoch, schema-derived erasure, export
- your rows: explicit upserts and deletes of item, episode and hidden state.
  No call infers a delete, so the prune invariant lives on the client
- cron: nightly export of everything a provider cannot give back to R2, the
  TMDB refresh inside its six-month cap, one calendar month per run

Sixteen site modules run in the Worker unchanged. verify-derive.mjs derives
every pool item with the Worker's code and compares it with what the site
stored: 4,506 of 4,507 identical, the one difference being the site's own
cache behind on a vote count.

For that, three changes to the site with no behaviour change there:
matcherPure.ts holds the two matcher rules that touch no database;
setIgdbTokenStore lets isolates share one Twitch token; httpFetch returns
HttpResponse, whose json() is typed any, because the Workers runtime types it
unknown. discoverIgdbUpcoming and fetchIgdbGamePage take an optional "card"
shape so the calendar does not parse forty full game payloads.

Measured on the live Worker: reads 1 to 4 ms of CPU, a 150-row delta page
3 ms. Paths that fetch from a provider run 4 to 7 ms warm and 10 to 20 ms on
a cold isolate against the free plan's 10 ms. None was terminated; if error
1102 appears the fix is Workers Paid. The seed cost 79,770 row writes, exactly
the figure predicted from the schema.

141 tests, run inside workerd against a local D1. Removing any of seven key
guards (audience pin, CSRF, epoch check, type in the link lookup, user scope
on a delete, the kv export skip, the fetch budget) fails them.
